test_title: PYST 21: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 13 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: When appointing judges to the High Courts, the President of India is required to consult which officials apart from the Chief Justice of India and the Chief Justice of the respective State?

options.text: The members of the State Legislature

solution:
The correct answer is __**The State Governor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Under Article 217 of the Indian Constitution, the President is required to consult the Chief Justice of India, the Chief Justice of the respective High Court, and the **Governor of the concerned State** before appointing judges to the High Courts.
 
• The role of the State Governor in this process is advisory, and the final decision is made by the President.
 
• The consultation process ensures the appointment of qualified and unbiased individuals to the judiciary, maintaining the integrity of the judicial system.
 
• The Chief Justice of India plays a critical role in providing recommendations to the President based on merit and judicial expertise.
 
• This constitutional provision is designed to promote a collaborative process involving key stakeholders in the judiciary and executive.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 217 of the Constitution of India:**

 
 
• It deals with the appointment and conditions of service of High Court judges.
 
• The President appoints judges after consultation with the Chief Justice of India, the Governor of the concerned state, and sometimes other judges as deemed necessary.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Chief Justice of India:**
 
 
• The Chief Justice of India provides recommendations to the President, ensuring judicial appointments are based on merit and integrity.
 
• This role is crucial for maintaining the independence of the judiciary.
 
 
 
• **High Court Judges:**
 
 
• They are responsible for adjudicating cases and upholding the Constitution within their respective jurisdictions.
 
• High Court judges hold office until the age of 62.
 
 
 
• **Governor's Advisory Role:**
 
 
• The Governor of the state provides input during the consultation process, representing the state’s interests.
 
• While the Governor’s role is advisory, the President has the final say in judicial appointments.
